chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام. I said: Tell me, if a drinker of nabīdh is seized but he has not become intoxicated, is he to be flogged eighty lashes? He said: No. And every intoxicant is haram (forbidden).
So the explanation in this also is taqiyyah, according to what we have stated earlier. As for what he narrated:

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةُ: dissimulation for protection under particular circumstances

ai.seo_question: Is a person punished with eighty lashes for drinking nabīdh if he did not become intoxicated?
ai.summary: This report addresses the legal ruling concerning one who drinks nabīdh without becoming intoxicated, and it states that such a person is not to be flogged with eighty lashes in this narration. At the same time, the Imam عليه السلام affirms the general principle that every intoxicant is haram (forbidden), while the compiler notes that the ruling here is understood under taqiyyah.
